title.narrative: Commercialization of IP: Rise in entrepreneurship and technology transfer enabled by an improved framework for commercialization of IP
Commercialization of IP: Rise in entrepreneurship and technology transfer enabled by an improved framework for commercialization of IP

target.value: Commercialization of IP: Rise in entrepreneurship and technology transfer enabled by an improved framework for commercialization of IP

actual.value:
Building on the SSC project, the Embassy of Denmark in a collaboration between Trade Council and IPR Counsellor organised visits at Innovation Centre DK and two large Danish companies with sites in Bangalore (LM Wind Power and Maersk) in May 2022.
The joint IP commercialization conference held in May 2022 had participation from several stakeholders representing the private sector thereby extending the relationship to them. The published report “IP Commercialization in an interconnected world” also comprises valuable input from the private sector, which can be built upon in the future.
There is a good working relationship between the trade department and the IP Counsellor, and when relevant, the IP counsellor supports with network or advise related to IPR. Furthermore, the previous IP Counsellor has helped to create a link between the India Denmark Business Association (IDBA) and the India IP Helpdesk (EU initiative) which provides guidance on IP related matters to European SMEs in In

target.value: Commercialization of IP: Rise in entrepreneurship and technology transfer enabled by an improved framework for commercialization of IP

actual.value: In April of 2023, the IP counsellor participated in a synergy workshop arranged by the Trade Council in Bangalore. This contributed both to creating awareness about the presence of the counsellor in the embassy and to discussions about concrete collaborative initiatives. Similarly, the sector counsellor participated in the regional TC meeting in December and presented the SSC-project for the regional colleagues. After the synergy workshop and regional meeting, the sector counsellor has provided general sector information in meetings with TC clients. The IP counsellor participated in Indo-Danish Business Association (IDBA) meetings in April and December and answered questions from IDBA members at a dedicated IPR-table in the December-meeting. An IPR-focussed IDBA-meeting with representatives from Danish and Indian authorities had been discussed but was ultimately postponed indefinitely. In October, DKPTO hosted an event for SMEs on “Doing business in India”.

target.value: Commercialization of IP: Rise in entrepreneurship and technology transfer enabled by an improved framework for commercialization of IP

actual.value: Joint activities were carried out with the objective of collecting knowledge and building relationships between the IP authorities and other key stakeholders in the IP commercialization ecosystem in India and DK. This work has progressed well and at the end of 2021 the first joint report on policy options to strengthen commercialization of IP was about to be finalized. Since IP commercialization is an innovation agenda, the report and the other activities feeding into it have been developed and carried out in collaboration with ICDK and the Ministry of Science and Higher Education in DK. Furthermore, a tailored online course on IP in general and IP tools for India’s TISC was carried out by DKPTO and 13 Indian officials participated in the tailor-made DFC course on Fostering Innovation and IP commercialization in DK. Combined, these activities have made a significant impact in supporting CIPAM/DPIIT towards obtaining the position as nodal agency in the ecosystem.

title.narrative: Exchange best practice on IPR enforcement
Strategy/model for enhanced cooperation between IP actors in India developed.

target.value: strategy/model for enhanced cooperation between IP actors in India.

actual.value: Outcome B has proved more challenging, especially with regards to interactions with enforcement authorities which have not yet materialized despite several attempts in 2021. Early in 2021, Denmark sought to initiate the joint work to establish an awareness raising strategy for CIPAM, and a few good workshops were carried out to kick start the collaboration. However, changing priorities in CIPAM (coupled with the onset of the second wave) meant that this was not prioritized for the remainder of 2021.

target.value: strategy/model for enhanced cooperation between IP actors in India.

actual.value: The first initiatives to conduct awareness and outreach activities at higher education institutions were taken in 2022. Specifically, DKPTO actively participated in a National IP Awareness Mission (NIPAM) event at Noida University in November 2022 for more than 200 students. Furthermore, 2022 has allowed for direct relationship building with external stakeholders which could be potential collaborators in future awareness raising and outreach activities.

title.narrative: Develop and implement quality management structures for patents and trademarks
Quality management structures documentation meets ISO 9001 standards

actual.value: Progress on Outcome A has continued to be largely carried by the Quality Management System (QMS) track (A.1), where three physical missions and a number of online sessions were conducted in 2023. In collaboration with the Indian side, the DKPTO-team has prepared a report detailing resource requirements for achieving a QMS in line with ISO 9001 standards for an organisation the size of the IPO. This will help the IPO to allocate resources and focus on implementing the QMS, which is a stated focus area for the IPO in the financial year 2024-25.

The theoretical groundworks have been completed, and the collaboration is now focused on implementing QMS in accordance with ISO 9001 principles in the Indian patent department. This is a major task, and will require much attention in 2022 as well. An important achievement in 2021 is the demonstrated recognition of the value of the collaboration with Denmark on QMS, and commitment at highest level to implement QMS in accordance with ISO 9001 in the Indian Patent Office. Due to covid-related challenges, other activity-streams under this outcome have been given lower priority, and only a few introductory activities have been carried out.

There has been good progress towards outcome A, especially with regards to output 1 on Quality Management System (QMS). The theoretical groundworks have been completed, and the collaboration is now focused on implementing QMS in accordance with ISO 9001 principles in all the different Indian IPR departments. This is a major task, and it will require much attention in 2023 as well.
